title: Partitioning a 4TB Postgres table without downtime
excerpt: We moved a 4.2TB events table to declarative partitioning while serving 12k writes/sec. Covers the pg_partman setup, the attach-with-check trick that avoids the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, and the two places where our plan still blocked for 40 seconds.

title: PgBouncer in transaction mode: what actually breaks
excerpt: Prepared statements, session variables, advisory locks and LISTEN/NOTIFY all behave differently under transaction pooling. Includes the pool_size formula we landed on after three incidents and a table of which client libraries cope.

title: Why your batch size is wrong
excerpt: A short argument that ingest batch sizes are usually tuned against throughput on an idle database and then never revisited under lock contention. Includes measurements at 100, 1k and 10k rows per COPY.

title: Understanding Postgres lock queues
excerpt: Reference documentation for every lock mode, the conflict matrix, and how a queued ACCESS EXCLUSIVE request blocks every reader behind it. Kept as a lookup table rather than a narrative.

title: The 2026 State of JavaScript survey results
excerpt: Framework satisfaction, retention and usage across 34,000 respondents. Signals bundler consolidation and a continued shift toward server components.

title: How we cut p99 ingest latency by 60%
excerpt: Our write path queued behind autovacuum on the hot table. Walks through the flamegraphs, the autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit change, and why the fix that worked was reducing transaction duration rather than adding hardware.

title: Staff engineer archetypes, five years on
excerpt: Revisiting the tech lead / architect / solver / right hand framing with what has held up and what has not since the book.

title: Announcing Acme Cloud DB 4.0
excerpt: Version 4.0 is generally available with a redesigned console, faster cold starts, and new regions in Mumbai and São Paulo. Pricing unchanged.

title: Connection pooling patterns for serverless Postgres
excerpt: Compares client-side pools, PgBouncer, and HTTP-based drivers under bursty lambda traffic, with measured connection setup costs for each and guidance on pool sizing when instance count is not under your control.

title: A visual guide to MVCC bloat
excerpt: Illustrated walkthrough of tuple visibility, dead tuples, and how long-running transactions pin the xmin horizon and stall vacuum across the whole cluster.

title: Hiring: we are looking for a Staff Platform Engineer
excerpt: Join our platform team. Competitive equity, remote-friendly within EU timezones, and a hardware budget.

title: Rust ownership explained through database transactions
excerpt: An analogy-driven essay: borrow checking as two-phase locking. More about teaching Rust than about databases, but the transaction framing is unusually clear.

title: COPY vs INSERT vs multi-row INSERT: measured
excerpt: Benchmarks all three ingest paths at several row widths on identical hardware, with WAL volume per method and the point where COPY stops winning because of index maintenance.

title: The case against microservices for small teams
excerpt: Argues that the coordination cost of service boundaries exceeds the scaling benefit below roughly thirty engineers, with three case studies of teams that consolidated back to a monolith.

title: Postgres 18 release notes
excerpt: Complete changelog: asynchronous I/O for sequential scans, improved partition pruning at execution time, skip-scan for btree indexes, and the full list of incompatibilities to check before upgrading.

title: What I learned running a 12-hour incident
excerpt: A first-person account of a long outage: handoffs, the comms cadence that worked, and the decision to stop debugging and fail over that should have come four hours earlier.

title: Designing idempotent ingest pipelines
excerpt: Dedup keys, watermarks, and exactly-once claims examined honestly. Includes the upsert pattern against a Postgres sink and what happens to it under a partitioned table with a non-unique partition key.

title: CSS container queries in production
excerpt: Six months of shipping container queries in a design system, including the fallback strategy for the two browsers that still lag.

title: Tail latency is a distribution, not a number
excerpt: Why tracking p99 alone hides bimodal behaviour, with heat-map examples from production systems and the instrumentation needed to see it.

title: Our migration from MongoDB to Postgres
excerpt: Six-month migration write-up: the dual-write period, how we validated row counts, the JSONB schema that replaced our documents, and the three queries that got slower.
